must_identify.item: The api crash loop is caused by redis being unavailable, not by the api itself
must_identify.evidence: All api replicas depend on Redis per-request and on startup; this caused 503s on every `/items` call from the "healthy" api pods [13, 15] and caused any api pod that restarted (via a `restartedAt` annotation applied at 21:23:31Z [7]) to crash-loop on its eager Redis startup check [6, 7, 13]. The api Deployment itself is unchanged between revisions 1 and 2 aside from the restart annotation [8, 19, 20], ruling out an application code or image change as a contributing factor.

must_identify.item: redis is Pending because its PVC requests storage class fast-ssd, which does not exist
must_identify.evidence: The cluster only has the `standard` (rancher.io/local-path) StorageClass; `fast-ssd` does not exist, so the PVC could never bind and provisioning failed [9, 11].

notes: The RCA has no remediation section. It implies the cause but never explicitly recommends switching the PVC to the `standard` StorageClass or reverting the redis change. A reviewer may want to confirm whether a stated fix is required.

reviewer_ai.reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 subagent (AI review, not a person)
reviewer_ai.notes: Agree with the judge. The redis Deployment YAML (Recreate strategy, PVC with fast-ssd), the storage class list, the empty redis endpoints, the FailedScheduling 'unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims' event and the 503s on both frontend pods are all in the tool output. The absolute timestamp 21:23:58Z for the redis pod deletion is derived from relative event ages and cannot be checked exactly, but nothing important depends on it. No fix is recommended.

fix_from_suggestions.reason: Rolling redis back to the pre-PVC revision removes the change that added the nonexistent fast-ssd PVC, which is an acceptable fix. Redis can then schedule and get endpoints, and the api pods recover without changes to api.
